$description: Olympia component tokens. Says which role token each part of a badge, pill, chip, button, card or focus ring reads, per variant and state. Read this before designing anything. It carries NO density — padding, height and gap are each product's call, because a marketing site and a dApp table need different ones. Every variant is exhaustive by construction: a status value with no variant here has no color, which is the point. A call-site ternary or string equality on a status name silently gives every new value the else-branch's color; this map cannot, because adding a value means adding a row.

focus.$description: Non-negotiable. Every interactive element on every surface gets a visible keyboard-focus indicator. WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7 and 1.4.11 — the ring is a non-text element and needs 3:1 against what it sits on.

badge.$description: A non-interactive status label. Tinted background, no border, pill radius. The text color IS the accent; the background is that same accent at 10% over the surface — which is why each accent was solved against its own tint rather than against the page.

requires-label.$description: HARD REQUIREMENT, WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.1. A badge always renders its status as TEXT; the color is redundant reinforcement and never the carrier. This is not a style preference — it is the only thing that makes these variants distinguishable to a color-blind reader. Measured with scripts/check-contrast.mjs: under deuteranopia and protanopia, which affect about 1 in 12 men, several of these variants lose over 90% of their chromatic separation from one another. In light mode the error/warning pair retains 6% of its hue difference and almost no lightness difference. No choice of colors fixes that while brand green and treasury amber stay where they are, so the label is the fix. A bare colored dot, a color-only legend, or an icon with no accessible name is a conformance failure, not a design choice.

tint-alpha.$description: Changing this invalidates every measured badge ratio. Re-run scripts/check-contrast.mjs if you do.

variant.$description: Meaning first, hue second. The house convention is: violet = Ethereum upgrade tracks, green = ETC-native, gray = maintenance or neutral, amber = treasury surfaces only.

neutral.$description: Maintenance, unknown, or no status. The default — never leave a value uncolored, give it this.

brand.$description: ETC-native. The green is the brand, so this is the strongest positive signal available.

treasury.$description: Treasury and financial data. RESERVED — amber appears on treasury surfaces and nowhere else. Do not use it as a general warning; --color-warning is its own token.

signaling.$description: Signaling and advisory, where the outcome is not binding.

pill.$description: A bordered label, usually carrying a count or a filter. Same radius as a badge, but a visible boundary instead of a tint — so the BORDER is the thing that must clear 3:1 (SC 1.4.11), not just the text.

disabled.$description: Exempt from 1.4.3 by SC exception, but keep the border perceivable so the control's shape still reads.

chip.$description: Interactive and dismissible — a selected filter, a tag on an input. Unlike a badge it takes focus, so it carries the focus ring and every state below.

dismiss.$description: The x. It is a graphical object and needs 3:1, and it needs a non-color affordance — an accessible name — because its meaning is carried by shape alone.

primary.$description: The label sits on the brand green, so it is measured against THAT, not against the page. bg-primary is the right label because it inverts with the theme, and the two themes need OPPOSITE labels: on dark-theme #00ffae a near-black label measures 14.62:1 while white measures 1.32:1, and on light-theme #007a53 it reverses — near-white 5.13:1, near-black 3.59:1. Measured across base/hover/active in both themes: 5.13 to 14.62:1, all passing. Do not hardcode a white label.
